text: A man who beat his wife or child, laid violent hands, he said, on what was most sacred; and a good husband he reckoned worthy of more praise than a great senator; and he admired the ancient Socrates for nothing so much as for having lived a temperate and contented life with a wife who was a scold, and children who were half-witted.
author: Plutarch
speaker: Cato the Elder
translation: John Dryden et al., rev. Arthur Hugh Clough, 1864
